title: Exercise authored personal content through the existing browser product paths

scope.subject: Playwright acceptance for bilingual authored discovery, Places navigation, and canonical Personal deep links

research_summary: Reuse the repository's existing Playwright browser harness, runtime cleanliness observer, YEIS wait helpers, Navigator UI, and URLSearchParams/History deep-link contract. The acceptance slice should prove that authored metadata travels through the actual product rather than creating an authoring-only preview route: English and Chinese authored names search the same canonical item, Places can open it, and a shareable personal:<contentId> URL reloads to the same destination. No additional browser runner, router, mock universe, or custom CDP harness is needed.

sources.finding: Playwright's existing locator and web-first assertion model is sufficient to verify Navigator results, URL state, product data attributes, and rendered content without adding another browser harness.
The existing single-page destination query parameter can represent canonical Personal content deep links and can be asserted directly after navigation and reload.

search_ladder.conclusion: No domain-specific authored-content acceptance product is needed because Personal Universe already owns the running product and only needs tests through its existing UI.
Reuse Playwright Test for browser lifecycle/assertions and the existing browser URL contract for shareable destination state.
Existing repository helpers already provide YEIS readiness, runtime cleanliness, and Navigator opening, so no additional testing subsystem is required.
The test can reuse existing locators and HTML data attributes; no new test component or fixture package is required.

candidates.name: Existing Personal Universe Playwright product harness
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 Playwright tooling plus project-owned tests
candidates.reason: It already boots the real app, waits for YEIS, observes runtime failures, opens Navigator, and asserts WebGL/navigation state, so authored-content acceptance should extend the same suite.

candidates.name: Existing URLSearchParams and History deep-link contract
candidates.source: Current UniverseApp destination query serialization and restore flow
candidates.reason: It is already the product's shareable navigation state, so canonical Personal content identity should be tested through that contract rather than a new router or test-only route.

decision.rationale: Extend the existing Playwright product suite and existing destination query contract. This exercises the real Search/Places/navigation/runtime path with no parallel test application, browser stack, or authoring-only destination model.
decision.fallback: If a future product surface cannot be reached through the existing browser harness, add only a shared Playwright helper inside the current test architecture rather than introducing a second runner.
